senses.definition: (nautical) The rigging of a sailing ship or other such craft.
Special equipment or gear used for a particular purpose.
examples: The climbers each had a different rig for climbing that particular rockface.
We used a ground-level rig to safely learn how to tile a gable roof.

senses.definition: (US) A large truck, especially a semi-trailer truck.
examples: Every rig at the truckstop had custom-made mud-flaps.

(transitive, manufacturing) To move (a heavy object) with the help of slings, hoists, block and tackle, levers, or similar equipment.

senses.definition: (transitive, informal) To dress or clothe in some costume.
(transitive) To make or construct something in haste or in a makeshift manner.
(transitive) To manipulate something dishonestly for personal gain or discriminatory purposes.

senses.definition: (algebra, ring theory) An algebraic structure similar to a ring, but without the requirement that every element have an additive inverse.
examples:
2004, Jerzy Marcinkowski (editor), Computer Science Logic: 18th International Workshop, CSL 2004, Proceedings, Springer, LNCS 3210, page 17,
It follows that for each object A its endomorphisms End_C(A) = C(A,A) has the structure of what is now called a rig, that is to say a (commutative) ring without negatives.

quotes.text: The set of natural numbers N with the usual operations of addition and multiplication is a rig, but not a ring. The set of integers Z is a ring. For a rig/ring (R,0,+,1,−), the set of polynomials R[x] on a generator x with the usual operations of addition and multiplication is also a rig/ring.
